subject: animation
intro: Animation leads into the screen industries' picture-making jobs — animating characters and effects, designing assets, editing sequences, and eventually directing teams that ship films, series and games.

roles.title: Special Effects Artists and Animators
roles.what: Create the movement and imagery in films, series and games: animate characters and creatures, build visual effects, texture and light shots, and work shot by shot to a director's brief and a production deadline.
roles.where: The twelve principles, walk cycles and acting, 3D rigging and pose-to-pose work, and the pipeline unit's layout, lighting and compositing are exactly the daily craft of this job.

roles.title: Graphic Designers
roles.what: Communicate visually: design logos, title cards, key art and marketing materials, develop style frames and campaign looks, and deliver consistent imagery across print and digital platforms.
roles.where: Unit 5's shape language and appeal, model-sheet consistency, and the design-for-movement topics give designers the character-forward visual thinking titles and key art need.

roles.title: Art Directors
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree, plus years of design experience
roles.what: Own the visual style of a production: set the look, direct designers and animators, approve concept art and final frames, and keep the imagery coherent and on schedule across a whole studio pipeline.
roles.where: Unit 8's directing-animation and pitch content, and the pipeline unit's studio roles and workflows, describe the leadership ladder from artist to art director this course maps out.

roles.title: Film and Video Editors
roles.what: Cut the story together: assemble footage, trim and sequence shots for rhythm and clarity, sync sound, grade and composite, and revise cuts through rounds of director and client feedback.
roles.where: Unit 4's animatic and leica-reel work — timing a story through an edit — and the post-production topics of the pipeline unit are the core skills editors use daily.

roles.title: Producers and Directors
roles.entry: Bachelor's degree, plus years of production experience
roles.what: Run productions from script to screen: develop and pitch projects, plan budgets and schedules, direct performances and review shots, and make the call on every cut before delivery.
roles.where: Unit 8's directing, pitches and pilots unit, plus the storyboard-to-animatic sequence of unit 4, is the production leadership pathway this role climbs.
